problem: Zero-shot MLLM VLN agents run open-loop with a single static instruction. Once perceptual aliasing, sensor noise or odometry drift pushes them off course, they have no way to recover. Existing dialogue-driven VLN uses dialogue only as extra planning context, is trained on simulated data, and assumes perfect, instant communication.
motivation: Humans who get lost describe their surroundings and ask for directions. Robots lack this help-seeking behaviour, which makes them brittle in real deployment. The authors treat dialogue as an operational error-recovery channel that can be attached to any existing agent.
key_idea: A model-agnostic module monitors agent kinematics (looping or divergence) and, on a trigger, has an MLLM turn the egocentric views into a grounded help query. An oracle or human answers with a relative-bearing hint, which is injected into the agent's prompt so it can re-plan.
insight: Sparse, targeted triggers beat frequent ones: the Deviation trigger gives SR 66.0, while the Hybrid trigger (23.1% query rate) drops to 54.0, which the authors call intervention fatigue. Stronger agents such as GTA show an inverted-U response to periodic hint frequency, while NavGPT degrades roughly linearly as hints get sparser. A clean, action-centric history also pairs better with egocentric hints than MapGPT's absolute coordinates (VLNVerse SR 67.02 vs 84.60 for NavGPT). Caveat: the hints come from an oracle that uses GT goal position, so the large gains reflect privileged information.
method: Base agent: frozen zero-shot MLLM agents (NavGPT, GTA, MapGPT) take four-view RGB-D observations and output pixel-coordinate or waypoint targets; T2E is plugged in without changing them.
Repeat trigger C_rep: fires when the agent has visited the current position (radius 0.5 m) at least 3 times.

Deviation trigger C_away: fires when the mean distance to goal over a sliding window of k=2 steps exceeds the previous window's mean. It uses GT goal position and is the best trigger. Hybrid (OR of both) and Periodic (every 5 steps) triggers are also studied.

Vision-Language Translator: an MLLM summarises the RGB-D views, infers the likely failure mode (loop, dead end, ambiguous intersection) and writes a short query grounded in visible landmarks and relative directions.

Oracle guide: computes the relative turn angle from the agent heading to the goal bearing and replies with the direction, angle and distance to goal, or 'very close to goal' below a threshold. A human-in-the-loop variant replaces this.
Prompt injection: the query and hint go into a 'Navigation Assistance' block placed between the history and the current observations, and the agent then re-plans.

Real robot: a Unitree Go2 with a servo-mounted depth camera runs the MLLM asynchronously, sending waypoints to the native point-to-point navigation stack. A human triggers hints only when a predefined failure is observed.

setting.backbone: Gemini 3.1 Pro (frozen) inside NavGPT / GTA agents; NavGPT and MapGPT also used on VLNVerse
setting.action_space: MLLM-chosen normalized pixel coordinates or relative waypoints, executed by a low-level controller
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D continuous, R2R-CE/RxR-CE) and VLNVerse; real Unitree Go2
setting.privileged: Oracle hints and the Deviation trigger use the GT goal position (bearing and distance to goal); a human guide is used in the real-world and human-in-the-loop runs

numbers_note: The split names for VLNVerse and the real-world tests are not stated in the paper, so 'val' and 'test' are assumptions. The ablation in Table 4 (Deviation SR 66.0 / SPL 49.4; Human-in-the-Loop SR 74.5 / SPL 61.2) conflicts with the headline numbers: the text and abstract state 66.0% SR while Table 1 shows 72.0% for the same setting (66.0 is the OSR there). The periodic-interval figure gives no numeric values.
results: Talk2Escape + GTA reaches 72.0 SR on the R2R-CE 100-episode subset, versus 48.8 for GTA and 64.2 for the best supervised method, Efficient-VLN. On RxR-CE SR rises from 46.2 to 62.9, but SPL falls from 39.3 to 34.2 and nDTW from 57.4 to 49.9. On the real Go2, SR goes from 40.0 (GTA) to 62.0.
limitations: Oracle hints use the GT goal position, so the results are not a fair zero-shot comparison. Evaluation is on small subsets (100 and 260 episodes), and the SR reported for R2R-CE is inconsistent between the text and the tables.
Path efficiency drops (SPL and nDTW) because recovery involves detours; a human guide with only static frames struggles to understand the robot's state ('asymmetric context').
Real-world trials use a human to trigger hints and give guidance, with few details on the number of trials.
